question: Does some textual connectors are compressed refer to an eligible underexplained interpretive connection or recognition corruption?
reviewerClarification: It refers only to an eligible argumentative compression, not recognition quality. Swinburne names Hebrews 12 as character formation and John 9 as suffering used to disclose divine power/goodness, but only briefly explains how those two examples support the broader inference that the Bible assigns distinct goods to distinct evils. The mapping/generalization is understandable yet underdeveloped. No corrupted connective word, transcript syntax, accent, or recognition uncertainty influenced the rating or rationale.
